title: TraceFormer: S-parameter Prediction Framework for PCB Traces based on Graph Transformer
problem: S-parameter modeling for PCB traces using numerical methods is computationally expensive and time-consuming. Solving governing equations becomes a critical bottleneck for signal integrity analysis in complex high-speed designs.
motivation: Signal integrity is critical for modern high-speed digital systems, and efficient S-parameter prediction is essential for practical PCB design workflows.
method: TraceFormer constructs a graph from PCB traces and tokenizes trace segments with geometric and topological information. A transformer encoder processes these tokens to produce PCB representations. Extraction networks jointly predict four types of complex-valued S-parameters, achieving R² >0.99 up to 15 GHz for 4-port designs.
key_novelty: Using graph transformers to tokenize PCB trace geometry and topology for efficient deep learning-based S-parameter prediction, replacing expensive numerical simulation.
contributions: TraceFormer framework combining graph representation and transformer architecture for S-parameter prediction
Graph-based tokenization scheme capturing geometric and topological features of PCB traces
High-accuracy predictions with R² >0.99 and eye diagram errors below 4.2%
Significant computational speedup over traditional numerical methods for signal integrity analysis

metrics.accuracy: R² >0.99 up to 15GHz; eye diagram width error <3.1%, height error <4.2%

limitations: Not discussed in the provided abstract.
primary_theme: ML-based S-parameter prediction for PCB signal integrity
